newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $15-$20 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $15-$20 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $15 to $20 per tonne higher on Monday, in line with gains in London overnight.

London cocoa futures rose in light trade early Monday, helped by weakness in the British pound. At the midday break, LIFFE December was up eight stg, to 1,039 stg, after trading in a 1,040-1,027 stg range.
Traders also said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report, which showed speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long 12,081 lots as of August 12, could help buoy the market.
The decline in the speculative net long position in line with expections, but some traders said speculators now had room to beef up their long positions.
""A month ago the spec net long position was more than 30,000," said one dealer. "The funds are more than capable of buying this market again."
In the two weeks ended August 12 the CFTC data showed non-commercial long positions decreased by 3,154 lots, to 16,245 lots. Non-commercial short positions increased by 2,674 lots, to 6,693 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 4,768 lots, to 68,147 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 2,594 lots, to 80,228 lots.
Nonreportable long positions increased by 561 lots, to 15,601 lots and nonreportable short positions increased by 2,095 lots, to 13,072 lots.

Friday, New York cocoa ended mixed in switch-dominated trading. September, which enters delivery period today, rose $1 a tonne, to $1,486. Active December closed $4 weaker, at $1,512, after ranging from $1,531 to $1,510. The back months finished unchanged to down $2.
On the charts, traders said December continued to face resistance at $1,532, with the next level seen at $1,543-$1,54. On the downside, support was seen near $1,510.
